cparsDisclaimer: All CPARS ratings shown are estimated — public data inference. Direct CPARS access is government-restricted; ratings are inferred from public award data, agency reporting, and reference confirmations, never pulled from the CPARS system of record.

overview.relevanceSummary: Three own-company references span the exact discriminators: same-agency DHS cybersecurity (Exceptional), cloud migration at scale (Army, Very Good), and FedRAMP compliance (Treasury, Very Good). Two partner references close the data-migration and ServiceNow capability gaps. The reference set covers evaluation factors M.1–M.3; M.4 (Transition & Staffing) has no dedicated past-performance reference and is flagged.

covered: M.1 — Technical Approach (cloud migration, ZTA, FedRAMP)
M.2 — Management Approach (program management track record)

uncovered.note: No past-performance reference specifically substantiates a transition-in / staffing-ramp narrative. The DHS CISA reference touches it tangentially; Staffing-tab data (transition plans, LOIs) is the better source. Flagged to Staffing.

fair.facts: DHS CISA cybersecurity modernization, $12.5M, 2023–present, CPARS Exceptional (estimated — public data inference). COR Michelle Adams confirmed as a reference. Same department, same security regime as this pursuit.
fair.analysis: This is the strongest possible reference: same agency, active (not historical), and the highest CPARS band. It directly substantiates WT-03 (mission-embedded zero trust) and D-04 (same-department experience). Performance highlights — ZTA Level 3 in 8 months, 15-minute MTTD — map to the M.1 technical-approach evaluation.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 An active Exceptional rating with a confirmed COR willing to speak is the rarest and most defensible evidence class an evaluator can verify. The incumbent's known DHS performance issues make this contrast sharper if surfaced carefully.
fair.recommendations: PP-01-R1: Use as the lead past-performance reference. · PP-01-R2: Pre-brief COR Michelle Adams on likely evaluator questions. · PP-01-R3: Pull the ZTA and MTTD metrics into the M.1 narrative.

envelope.aiReasoning: Highest-confidence reference: same agency, active, Exceptional CPARS (estimated), confirmed COR. The strongest card in the deck.

sources.label: Public award data — DHS CISA (estimated CPARS)

fair.facts: U.S. Army enterprise cloud migration, 2022–2025, CPARS Very Good (estimated — public data inference). COR Lt. Col. Whitaker confirmed. Largest prior data migration: 180 applications, CloudPathfinder-assessed, completed ahead of schedule.
fair.analysis: The proof point for WT-01 (accelerated mission outcomes) and D-02 (CloudPathfinder). 180 applications is directly comparable to the DHS 340+ portfolio scale, and the CloudPathfinder dependency-catch metric (23 undocumented dependencies found) substantiates the migration-factory claim in Solutioning sol-1.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 This reference carries one flagged weakness from the data call: the FinOps savings figures need independent verification (DC-001-02). Cite the migration metrics freely; hold the FinOps dollar figures until verified to avoid an evaluator challenge.
fair.recommendations: PP-02-R1: Use as reference #2, anchoring the migration-at-scale narrative. · PP-02-R2: Complete the FinOps savings verification flagged in DC-001-02 before citing those figures. · PP-02-R3: Foreground the 180-app / 23-dependency CloudPathfinder metrics in M.1.

envelope.aiReasoning: Strong, directly comparable migration reference with a confirmed COR; confidence is held below the 90s by the unverified FinOps savings figures flagged in DC-001-02.

fair.facts: Treasury IT modernization, $6.2M, 2021–2024, CPARS Very Good (estimated — public data inference). COR Karen Blackwell confirmed. Narrative centers on FedRAMP compliance achievement.
fair.analysis: A supporting reference for WT-02 (zero-day FedRAMP compliance) and D-01. Less directly relevant to cloud-migration scope than PP-01/PP-02, so it is positioned as supporting evidence rather than a lead — strongest on the compliance dimension.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 Positioning matters: leading with Treasury would dilute the cloud-migration story. Used deliberately to reinforce the FedRAMP discriminator where an evaluator probes compliance depth.
fair.recommendations: PP-03-R1: Use as a supporting reference on the FedRAMP/compliance factor. · PP-03-R2: Keep the narrative tight on compliance; do not over-claim migration relevance.

envelope.aiReasoning: Solid Very Good reference with a confirmed COR, but lower relevance to the core migration scope caps its weight — correctly a supporting, not lead, reference.

fair.facts: GovFlow Technologies — DHS ServiceNow integration, $3.1M, 2022–2024, CPARS Very Good (estimated — public data inference). Partner-provided reference. Same agency, same platform as the CG-02 requirement.
fair.analysis: Closes the CG-02 capability gap (DHS-specific ServiceNow). Same-instance experience is exactly what evaluators familiar with the DHS OCIO ServiceNow environment will probe for. The weakness is governance: GovFlow's TA is unsigned (term sheet), so this cannot yet be cited as a team reference of record.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 A partner-provided rating is weaker evidence than an own-company CPARS — it should be corroborated against public award data before it enters the proposal, and it depends on the GovFlow TA executing.
fair.recommendations: PP-04-R1: Corroborate the GovFlow rating against public award data. · PP-04-R2: Cite as a team reference only after the GovFlow TA is executed. · PP-04-R3: Position as the CG-02 proof point in M.1.

envelope.aiReasoning: Relevant same-agency same-platform reference, but partner-provided (weaker class) and dependent on an unsigned TA. Confidence reflects both caveats.

fair.facts: DataBridge Analytics — USCIS data modernization, $4.2M, 2021–2023, CPARS Satisfactory (estimated — public data inference). Partner-provided. Demonstrates DHS-component data-migration and ETL experience (the CG-01 capability).
fair.analysis: Substantiates DataBridge's data-migration capability for CG-01 and sol-1's ETL factory. Two weaknesses: it is the lowest CPARS band of the reference set (Satisfactory, not Very Good/Exceptional), and it is partner-provided and dependent on DataBridge's unsigned TA. Use it for capability evidence, not as a quality discriminator.
fair.intelligence: 🔒 A Satisfactory rating is a double-edged citation — it proves capability but signals mediocre performance. Frame around the specific schema-migration experience (DHS HR Connect, TECS), not the overall rating.
fair.recommendations: PP-05-R1: Cite DataBridge for CG-01 capability, foregrounding the specific legacy-schema experience over the rating. · PP-05-R2: Corroborate against public award data. · PP-05-R3: Cite as a team reference only after the DataBridge TA executes.

envelope.aiReasoning: Weakest reference of the set: Satisfactory CPARS (estimated), partner-provided, and dependent on an unsigned TA. Useful for capability evidence but not as a quality signal — appropriately the lowest-confidence reference.
